field_summary:
WASHINGTON, Feb. 23, 2025 – LPK1, a company in Renton, Wash., is recalling approximately 303 pounds of ready-to-eat Caesar chicken wraps due to misbranding and an undeclared allergen, the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS) announced today. The product's individually packaged Caesar dressing contains fish (anchovies), a known allergen, which is not declared on the product label.

The ready-to-eat Caesar chicken wraps were produced on February 15, 2025, February 17, 2025, and February 19, 2025. The following products are subject to recall: [View Labels]:

  • 10 oz. clear clam shell containers containing “thoughtfully handmade just for you Chicken Caesar Wrap with parmesan cheese lettuce, Caesar dressing” (Chicken Caesar Wrap with Parmesan Cheese, Lettuce, Caesar Dressing, carefully made for you) with "best by" dates of FEB 21, FEB 23, FEB 25, and lot codes LPK1WA046, LPK1WA048, LPK1WA050 printed on the label.

The recalled products bear the establishment number “P2276” inside the USDA mark of inspection. These items were distributed to vending machines in office buildings in the state of Washington.

The problem was discovered by the company during routine review of ingredient labels as part of their quality assurance process. The establishment subsequently notified FSIS that the product may contain fish (anchovies), which is not declared on the label.

There have been no confirmed reports of adverse reactions due to consumption of these products. Anyone concerned about an illness should contact a healthcare provider.

FSIS is concerned that some product may be in vending machines in office buildings. Consumers who purchased these products are urged not to consume them and offices are urged not to serve them. These products should be discarded or returned to the vending machine owners.

FSIS conducts routine reviews of recall effectiveness to verify that companies notify their customers of a recall and follow appropriate steps to ensure that the product is no longer available to consumers.

Media with questions about the recall can contact Kristin Elder, Public Relations Specialist, H+K Strategies, at kristin.elder@hkstrategies.com. Consumers with questions about the recall can contact Ryan Calbreath, Quality Assurance Manager, LPK1, at 925-457-6738 or ryan.calbreath@compass-usa.com.

Consumers with food safety questions can call the USDA Meat and Poultry Hotline at 888-MPHotline (888-674-6854) or send an email to MPHotline@usda.gov. Consumers who need to report a problem with meat, poultry, or egg products can access the Electronic Consumer Complaint System 24 hours a day at https://foodcomplaint.fsis.usda.gov/eCCF/.
